rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 4 "The first piece of the picture", line 42: "In the full agent picture, this is the first piece: context." The slide's own header and the pieces it lists (tools, goals, checks, boundaries, loops) establish the picture in-chunk, and 'this' binds to 'context', the subject of the preceding slide 3. Chunk 2 line 24 "the second prompt" resolves to line 11 on chunk 1; chunk 5 line 51 "That's a guardrail" names its own referent in apposition. Harm (reader cannot resolve a referent) absent.

Closest: chunk 5 line 51 "That's your turn." points forward at the next exercise without naming a file or position; grep for 'opening lecture|earlier lecture|last module|the previous' in body view: 0 hits. No callback to another file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: chunk 5 line 47 "So far the context has been one message you typed." resolves to chunks 1-3 of the same file. No 'the X you did/saw/caught' reference to a module beat exists in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 "Same question, two answers": cue at line 15 "Before you read on, take a guess. What will it suggest?" precedes the Finnish reveal at line 17 "Claude suggests something Finnish"; the only outcome narrated above the cue is the Italian one (line 11), which is the control, not the guessed answer. Maintainer 2026-10-06 attests the ordering. Muted read: closest verbless lines are line 9 "Two Claude chat windows." and cover line 4 "The same question. Two answers. What makes the difference?" Harm of the rule (a scene that exists only in the trainer's mouth) is absent: lines 11 and 13 give the full verbed scene on the page and 'it' at line 15 binds to Claude (lines 9-13). Line 37 'A fact. A role. A preference. A constraint.' and line 35 'Heart-healthy. Low-sodium.' follow verbed sentences naming the set (carve-out). Rule question for the maintainer: line 4 is near-verbatim the rule's own canonical example; two suggestions filed.

Smallest chunk: chunk 4 line 42 "In the full agent picture, this is the first piece: context. Later you add tools, goals, checks, boundaries, and loops." carries a self-contained claim (context is the first of several pieces). Not a wait-state.

Closest: chunk 5 header "A file it reads every time" (line 44): 'it' is the agent, named at line 42 on the previous slide and in the body at line 49 'the agent reads'. Body delivers exactly the promised file-read-every-time idea. Chunk 2 header 'It reads the whole conversation every time' matches line 24.

Mechanical/judgement per sub-item. Not-X-Not-Y-Z: closest line 35 "Not because Claude knows medicine better than Italian cooking. You told it who you are" is a single 'Not because' then a positive, not a triple. Anaphora: line 37 "A fact. A role. A preference. A constraint." four distinct concrete kinds, each new content, not a repeated lead. Self-grading superlative: line 26 "every useful thing in this training is built on this one idea" is a structural claim, not 'one of the most useful moves'; no value-prop superlative. Number+retraction: none. Abstraction-noun stack: line 42 'the right world' single figurative noun, concrete enough. Verb triplets: none.
